name: STORM R1 TLR

origin.basis: ARISUN is a ZC Rubber (Zhongce, maker of Chaoyang) bicycle-tire brand; the official listing gives the brand as 朝阳 and the item code 艾瑞森H-908.

manufacturing.basis: The listing does not state the factory location.

positioning: Tubeless version of the STORM R1, 220 TPI at 25 and 28 mm and 330 TPI at 30 mm.
weight_basis: One owner weighed a 28C tubeless tire at 269 g.

community.summary: A creator test found it seated with a floor pump and could be fitted by hand; no durability result.
Owner-measured 269 g at 28C, alongside the clincher; commenters cite fast wear for the R1 family.

availability.note: Sold in mainland China through an official Tmall store.

price_observations.conditions: Tmall list price before discounts ('优惠前') on 2026-11-01; the listing does not say whether the option is one tire or a pair.

caveats: Hookless compatibility and maximum pressure are not stated in the listing; follow your rim maker's limits.

One tubeless owner had both tires bulge by about 5,000 km and suspects an older batch; other bulge reports in the same threads do not say which version. Inspect the casing regularly. No independent lab test found.

image.shown: Folded 28C tubeless tire on a scale (269.3 g) in an owner's post; the sidewall reads ARISUN 风R, Tubeless Ready, 220 TPI, the tubeless version sold as the STORM R1.
image.alt: Folded ARISUN tubeless-ready road tire with its 220 TPI sidewall label on a scale

rights.usage_note: A photo from a public Xiaohongshu post, shown from Xiaohongshu with a link to the original post; no copy is stored or redistributed by this project, and no license is asserted.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded from the same seven Xiaohongshu posts reviewed on 2026-11-03 (not exhaustive). Counted only owners who said they ride the tubeless version or described sealant use; replies that did not say which version, seller replies, questions, hearsay and repeated comments by one owner were left out. No owner described riding it in the wet.

reports.summary: Holds corners better than the GP5000 S TR it replaced and rides comfortably, but is heavier and was slightly slower on repeated road segments; not a controlled test. Road conditions not stated.
Cuts from a rough road kept leaking through sealant, so the owner replaced it and found a Vittoria tubeless tire faster and trouble-free.
A pothole cut the front during a race and sealant could not close it; the owner fitted a tube to finish.

reports.exposure: About 5,000 km per tire, partly gravel
reports.summary: A sidewall puncture in the front would not seal and the tire was scrapped; the rear was still in good shape after the same distance.
Front and rear both bulged by about 5,000 km; the owner fitted them about a year earlier and suspects an older batch. Posted as a warning.
A large sideslip at a corner the owner had ridden hundreds of times, where an earlier GP5000 never slid. Road conditions not stated.

checks.note: Seven posts; two older posts are not yet re-checked owner by owner
